items.title: Section: A New Ground Opens — Six Reasons the Three Jewels Deserve Their Name

items.zh: 如是已說無心地決擇。聞所成慧地決擇，我今當說。謂由五處觀察所歸，乃可歸依。一、由身業清淨故；二、由語業清淨故；三、由意業清淨故；四、由於諸有情起大悲故；五、由成就無上法故。問：歸依
items.en: The Ground of Wisdom Attained through Hearing, within the chapter of decisive discernment. Thus I have already explained the decisive discernment of the Ground without Mind. I shall now explain the decisive discernment of the Ground of Wisdom Attained through Hearing. One should observe five aspects in what is taken as refuge before genuine refuge can be taken: purity of bodily conduct; purity of verbal conduct; purity of mental conduct; giving rise to great compassion towards all beings; and having accomplished the unsurpassed Dharma.

items.title: Section: A Teacher Who Watches Six Times Each Day and Night

items.zh: 有幾種？何緣但有爾所歸依？齊何緣故說能歸依？云何修行歸依之行？何等歸依所得功德？
items.en: The first aspect is purity of bodily conduct, free of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct. The second is purity of verbal conduct, free of falsehood, harsh speech, divisive speech, and idle chatter. The third is purity of mental conduct, free of greed, hatred, and delusion. The fourth is giving rise to great compassion towards all beings, regarding every being as an only child. The fifth is accomplishing the unsurpassed Dharma, perfect and complete awakening. I constantly know which beings practice the path and which do not, and teach the Dharma according to what each can receive. I always think to myself how I might lead beings into the unsurpassed path and swiftly accomplish the Buddha's own body.

items.title: Section: Four Reasons There Are Exactly Three Refuges

items.zh: 答：歸依有三種，謂佛法僧。四緣故有爾所歸依。一、由如來性極調善故；二、於一切種所調、能調善方便故；三、具大悲故。四、以一切財而興供養未將為喜，要以正行而興供養乃生歡喜。
items.en: Answer: there are three kinds of refuge, the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Four causes account for exactly this many refuges: the Buddha's own nature is perfectly tamed and good; the Buddha is skilful in every respect towards those to be tamed and the very means of taming them; the Buddha possesses great compassion; and the Buddha does not delight in offerings of mere wealth, but only in offerings made through genuine practice.

items.zh: 由如是故，彼所立法、彼弟子眾皆可歸依。

items.title: Section: Why the Buddha, and Not the Gods, Deserves to Be Called Teacher

items.zh: 齊四緣故說能歸依。一、知功德故；二、知差別故；三、自誓願故；四、更不說有餘大師故。當知歸依有四正行。一、親近善士，二、聽聞正法，三、如理作意，四、法隨法行。若有成就此四正行，乃名歸依。
items.en: Genuine refuge requires four conditions together: knowing the Buddha's virtues; knowing the difference between the Buddha and other teachers; one's own sincere vow; and there being no other teacher to prefer instead. One should know that refuge involves four correct practices: drawing near to a good friend, hearing the true Dharma, bringing correct attention to it, and practising the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma. Only one who accomplishes these four practices is genuinely called one who has taken refuge.

items.title: Section: Eight Marks of a Good Friend, and a Second Set of Four Practices

items.zh: 當知復有四種正行。一、諸根不掉，二、受學學處，三、悲愍有情，四、應時時間於三寶所勤修供養。
items.en: One should know there are also four further correct practices: the sense faculties not restlessly wandering; receiving and training in the training points; compassion for beings; and, day by day, diligently cultivating offering towards the Three Jewels.

items.title: Section: Eight Merits That Follow from Genuine Refuge

items.zh: 受歸依者獲四功德。一、獲廣大福，二、獲大歡喜，三、獲三摩地，四、獲大清淨。復獲四德。一、大護圓滿；二、於一切種邪信解障皆得輕微，或永滅盡；三、得入聰叡、正行正至、善士眾中，所謂大師、同梵行者；四、為於聖教淨信諸天歡喜愛念，
items.en: Those who take refuge gain four merits: vast blessing, great joy, concentration, and great purity. They also gain four further merits: complete protection; every obstacle rooted in wrong belief becoming markedly diminished or entirely gone; entry into the company of the wise, of correct practice, and of those who have arrived, namely the Teacher and fellow practitioners of pure conduct; and the delighted, loving regard of the gods who hold pure faith in the noble teaching.

items.zh: 謂彼天眾心生歡喜，唱如是言：我等成就三歸依故，從彼處沒來生此間；是諸人等今既成就多住歸依，亦當來我眾同分中。復次，由六種相，佛法僧寶差別應知。一、由相故；二、由業故；三、信解故；四、修行故；五、隨念故；六、生福故。云何相故三寶差別？謂自然覺悟相是佛寶，覺悟果相是法寶，隨他所教正修行相是僧寶。

items.title: Section: Born from the Buddha's Own Mouth — What Makes the Sangha One Body

items.zh: 云何業故三寶差別？謂轉正教業是佛寶，捨煩惱苦所緣境業是法寶，勇猛增長業是僧寶。云何信解故三寶差別？謂於佛寶，應樹親近承事信解；於法寶所，應樹希求證得信解；於僧寶所，應樹和合同一法性共住信解。
items.en: What is the distinction of the Three Jewels through function? Turning the true teaching is the Buddha's function; serving as the object relied on to abandon affliction and suffering is the Dharma's function; vigorous increase in practice is the Sangha's function. What is the distinction through faith and understanding? Towards the Buddha, one should cultivate faith through devoted closeness and service; towards the Dharma, faith through aspiring to realise it; towards the Sangha, faith through harmonious dwelling together in one and the same nature.

items.title: Section: Better to Suffer Every Pain Than Never Hear the Buddha's Name

items.zh: 云何修行故三寶差別？謂於佛寶，應修供養承事正行；於法寶所，應修瑜伽方便正行；於僧寶所，應修共受財法正行。云何隨念故三寶差別？應以餘相隨念佛寶，應以餘相隨念法寶，應以餘相隨念僧寶。謂是世尊，乃至廣說。
items.en: What is the distinction through practice? Towards the Buddha, cultivate the practice of offering and service; towards the Dharma, cultivate the practice of yogic skilful means; towards the Sangha, cultivate the practice of sharing wealth and Dharma in common. What is the distinction through recollection? Recollect the Buddha jewel, the Dharma jewel, and the Sangha jewel each through their own distinct aspect, namely that this is the World-Honoured One, and so extensively explained.

items.title: Section: Five Ways the Buddhist Path Outshines the Brahmin's

items.zh: 云何生福故三寶差別？謂於佛寶，依一有情生最勝福；於法寶所，即依此法生最勝福；於僧寶所，依多有情生最勝福。復次，由五法故，沙門、婆羅門勝劣差別。何等五法？一者、聞法，二者、戒法，三、攝受法，四、受用法，五、證得法。謂婆羅門所有聞法，義虛劣故，不示他故，文句隱故，是其下劣。沙門聞法與此相違，故是勝妙。又婆羅門所有戒法，隨何、隨分、隨其差別，開許害等，故是下劣。沙門戒法與此相違，故是勝妙。又婆羅門所攝受法，攝受障道田事、宅事、財貨事等，又復攝受妻子、奴婢、僮僕等類，故是下劣。沙門所有攝受之法，除離苦法，更無所有，故是勝妙。
items.en: What is the distinction through generating merit? Relying on the Buddha jewel, one being, the most supreme merit is generated; relying on the Dharma jewel, this very Dharma, the most supreme merit is generated; relying on the Sangha jewel, many beings, the most supreme merit is generated. There are also five factors distinguishing the superior from the inferior between renunciants and brahmins: the teaching heard, the precepts held, what is embraced, what is enjoyed, and what is realised. The brahmins' own teaching is empty, inferior, unshown to others, and obscure in wording, and so inferior; the renunciants' teaching is the reverse, and so superior. The brahmins' precepts permit various kinds of harm, and so are inferior; the renunciants' precepts are the reverse, and so superior. The brahmins embrace fields, houses, wealth, wives, servants, and slaves, and so are inferior; the renunciants embrace nothing beyond what frees one from suffering, and so are superior.

blocks.text: Fascicle 64 ascertains the Stage of What Is Learned Through Hearing, beginning with the "inner science": the three refuges.
Purity of body, speech, and mind, great compassion, and the unsurpassed Dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: each of the ninety-six other paths has its own refuge; only a Buddha accomplishes all of these.
The Buddha does not delight in offerings of mere wealth, only in offerings of genuine practice. Master Cháng Bǎi: to be able to tame is to give medicine suited to the illness.

subs.head: Why the Buddha, not the gods

blocks.text: Knowing the virtues, knowing the difference, one's own vow, and having no other teacher.
A good friend, hearing, correct attention, and practice according to the Dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: 法 refers to nirvāṇa, 隨法 to the eightfold path. True offering is diligent practice.

Master Cháng Bǎi: when one takes refuge, the gods who have faith are delighted and protect that person. (Untranslated, 0653a15: the gods say, "We were born here through the three refuges; these people too will join us"; and the three jewels differ in six ways: the Buddha is self-awakening, the Dharma the fruit of awakening, the Saṅgha those who practise as taught.)
The Buddha turns the teaching; the Dharma is what one relies on to abandon affliction; the Saṅgha grows vigorously. Master Cháng Bǎi: recollect each jewel's merits through its own aspect.
The teaching heard, the precepts held, what is embraced, what is enjoyed, and what is realised. Master Cháng Bǎi: what renunciants embrace is only what frees from suffering.
"The Buddha delights only in offerings of practice." Every offering of flowers points to this one.

quiz.q: What are the five aspects to observe in what is taken as refuge?
options: pure bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, great compassion towards beings, and the unsurpassed Dharma
a good friend, hearing, attention, practice in accordance with the Dharma, and training
knowing virtues, knowing difference, one's vow, no other teacher, and compassion
the teaching heard, precepts, what is embraced, enjoyed, and realised
quiz.why: The treatise lists purity of body, speech, and mind, great compassion, and the unsurpassed Dharma. These are marks of the one taken as refuge; the other options belong to the person taking refuge or to the renunciant-brahmin comparison.

quiz.q: Why, says Master Cháng Bǎi, should one observe the five aspects before taking refuge?
options: because the five are preconditions of ordination, examined by the community beforehand
to confirm that one's own three kinds of conduct are already free of fault
to compare with the ninety-six other paths; only a Buddha accomplished in the five may be relied upon
to choose which living good friend one will follow
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: each of the ninety-six other paths has its own object of refuge, so one compares them with the Buddha, and only a Buddha accomplished in these five may be taken as refuge. The five describe the refuge, not the one taking it.

quiz.q: What is the fourth of the causes accounting for this many refuges?
options: the Buddha's skill in every respect towards those to be tamed and the means of taming them
the Buddha delights not in offerings of wealth but only in offerings made through genuine practice
the Buddha's nature is perfectly tamed and good
the Buddha possesses great compassion
quiz.why: The treatise's fourth cause is that the Buddha does not delight in offerings of mere wealth, only in offerings made through genuine practice. Tamed nature, skill, and compassion are the first three.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain being able to tame?
options: giving medicine for the illness, knowing capacities, so that it truly cuts affliction
the Buddha uses supernormal power to remove beings' afflictions directly
the Buddha's own mind is gentle, and that alone is the taming
the Buddha sets precepts and binds disciples by communal rule
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: to be able to tame is to give medicine suited to the illness, knowing beings' capacities, so that it truly removes affliction and brings the noble path. The Buddha's own gentleness belongs to the first cause.

quiz.q: What four conditions together make genuine refuge?
options: the Buddha's tamed nature, skill, compassion, and delight in practice, four causes showing why the Buddha deserves refuge and so serving equally as the conditions for one who takes it
restrained faculties, studying the training points, compassion, offering
vast blessing, great joy, concentration, and great purity
knowing virtues, knowing the difference from other teachers, one's vow, and no other teacher to prefer
quiz.why: The treatise names knowing the virtues, knowing the difference, one's own vow, and no other teacher. The neighbouring lists give why there are three refuges, further practices, and the merits gained.

quiz.q: Which four correct practices must be accomplished to be called one who has taken refuge?
options: drawing near a good friend, hearing the true Dharma, correct attention, and practice in accordance with the Dharma
restrained faculties, training, compassion, and offering, which the treatise calls the real refuge while treating good friends and hearing as mere preparation that does not yet count as refuge at all
offering and service, yogic means, sharing wealth, and recollection
taking the refuges, keeping five precepts, generosity, and meditation
quiz.why: The treatise lists a good friend, hearing, correct attention, and practice in accordance with the Dharma, and says only one who accomplishes these is called one who has taken refuge. The next list adds further practices and replaces nothing.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 法 and 隨法 in practice in accordance with the Dharma?
options: 法 is the sūtra's words and 隨法 the commentary on them, so reading both is the practice
法 is the Buddha jewel and 隨法 the Sangha jewel
法 is nirvana; 隨法 is the eightfold path or the factors of awakening, the methods that realise it
法 is the renunciant's precepts and 隨法 the householder's
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 法 refers to nirvana, and 隨法 to the eightfold path or the thirty-seven factors of awakening, the methods one must practise to realise nirvana. The phrase therefore points to cultivation, not reading.

quiz.q: This is rendered "approval of the gods towards genuine faith in the noble teaching." What is confused?
options: the faith belongs to the gods: gods who have faith in the teaching cherish the one taking refuge
nothing: what the gods approve is faith itself, for the treatise means they like such faith apart from any person who takes refuge
諸天 should be spirits, not gods
joy and love are given in reversed order
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when one takes refuge, the gods who have pure faith in the teaching are delighted and cherish that person, who gains their protection. The English turns faith into what the gods approve, losing the point.

quiz.q: In the distinction through function, what is each jewel's function?
options: turning the teaching is the Buddha's, what abandons affliction the Dharma's, vigorous increase the Sangha's
vigorous increase is the Buddha's, turning the teaching the Dharma's, and abandoning affliction the Sangha's
closeness to the Buddha, aspiring to the Dharma, harmony with the Sangha
offering for the Buddha, yoga for the Dharma, sharing for the Sangha
quiz.why: The treatise assigns turning the teaching to the Buddha, the object for abandoning affliction to the Dharma, and vigorous increase to the Sangha. The other lists are the distinctions through faith and through practice. The heading listing six aspects is missing from the English, so numbering is not tested.

quiz.q: In the distinction through practice, what practice is cultivated towards the Dharma?
options: the practice of yogic skilful means
the practice of offering and service, since the Dharma is the most honoured of the three and the Buddha and Sangha merely transmit it
the practice of sharing wealth and Dharma in common
the practice of dwelling together in one nature
quiz.why: The treatise assigns offering and service to the Buddha, yogic means to the Dharma, and sharing wealth and Dharma to the Sangha. Dwelling together harmoniously belongs to the distinction through faith.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain yogic skilful means?
options: yoga means breath and posture, and means are the beginner's preparatory movements
yoga is chanting and means are mantras
yoga means correspondence: cultivating the calm and insight of the three vehicles that accord with the Dharma
yoga is copying sūtras and means are making images
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: yoga means correspondence, and the contemplative practice of the three vehicles is also called yoga, so cultivating the calm and insight that accord with the Dharma is called yogic skilful means.

quiz.q: By which five factors are renunciants and brahmins distinguished?
options: bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, compassion, and the unsurpassed Dharma
hearing, reflection, cultivation, precepts, concentration
caste, wealth, learning, appearance, incantation
the teaching heard, precepts, what is embraced, what is enjoyed, and what is realised
quiz.why: The treatise lists the teaching heard, the precepts held, what is embraced, what is enjoyed, and what is realised. Each is then compared, with the brahmins' side called inferior and the renunciants' superior.

quiz.q: Why does the treatise call the brahmins' teaching heard inferior?
options: it permits killing and the like in various degrees, and this is why the teaching heard is inferior
it embraces fields, wealth, wives, and servants
its meaning is empty and inferior, it is not shown to others, and its wording is obscure
it culminates only in the Brahma world and falls back
quiz.why: The treatise gives three reasons for the teaching heard: empty and inferior meaning, not shown to others, and obscure wording. Permitting harm concerns precepts, property concerns what is embraced, and the Brahma world concerns realisation.
